name: Capacitor-Grade BOPP/Dielectric Films
scope: Ultra-thin metallised BOPP/PET dielectric film for film capacitors (EV inverters and chargers, solar/wind inverters, grid capacitor banks, drives) and the Indian listed companies making, buying or adjacent to it.

summary.one_line: Three Indian listed companies make capacitor-grade film: Cosmo First, Jindal Poly (through its subsidiary JPFL Films) and SRF. New this week: a CRISIL report puts JPFL's operational capacitor-film capacity at 5,000 TPA after the fire, and DGTR has recommended anti-dumping duty on PET film. None of the three discloses capacitor-film revenue, and their valuations show no thematic premium.
key_points: IndexBox (28 Sep 2026) forecasts 6-9% annual growth in global dielectric capacitor-film demand over 2026-2035 (7.5% base case). It expects automotive power electronics to be the fastest-growing segment at 10-14% a year, and sees BOPP keeping 60-70% of volume (S1). Mordor's forecast for the finished plastic film capacitor market is slower: USD 2.58 bn in 2026 to USD 3.27 bn in 2031, a 4.86% CAGR (S2).
India is the world's 3rd-largest importer of capacitor metallised film. China accounts for 7,867 shipments versus 588 from Japan (S16), and China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1).

New this week: CRISIL's 18 May 2026 rating rationale for Jindal Poly says 5,000 TPA of capacitor-film capacity is operational at JPFL Films. It says one capacitor line restarted in H2 FY26, and that the Nashik site runs at ~35% of total capacity after the May 2025 fire (S10). The Rs 250 cr doubling announced in 2024 (S5) is still not confirmed as complete.

SRF commissioned phase 1 of its capacitor-grade BOPP plant at Indore (~Rs 277 cr) on 15 May 2026, with a ~Rs 6 cr phase 2 due in Sep 2026 (S11). On its Q1 FY27 call, management said approvals had been secured from several leading customers and expected early revenue late in Q2 FY27 (S12). Q2 results due in October will be the first check on that.

Cosmo First has made metallised capacitor-grade BOPP (2.5-12 micron) since Dec 2023, launched at ~750 MT/yr (S3). Its website now rates the metalliser at 900 MT/yr and says a second metalliser is being prepared (S4).

ECMS approvals now include three capacitor-film projects: SRF (polypropylene capacitor film, Rs 496 cr, Oct 2025) (S13), Dhruv Industries (metallised film, Mar 2026) (S14) and Capfilm India (metallised film for capacitors, Aug 2026) (S15). Across 106 applications, the scheme's approved investment totals Rs 69,548 cr (S15).

Jindal Poly has received two SEBI show-cause notices, dated 27 Apr 2026 (S9) and 6 Aug 2026 (S8), covering transactions, disclosures and governance. CRISIL keeps the company's ratings on 'Watch Negative' (S10).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: SRF has the newest dedicated capacity, with customer approvals secured and early revenue guided for late Q2 FY27 (S11, S12). On Screener's figures it trades at 34.1x P/E, so this small business is unlikely to move the stock (S25).

Cosmo First has been making the film longest among listed peers (since Dec 2023). Its 'series' metallised grade targets renewable-energy and EV capacitors (S3, S4). It trades at 13.0x P/E and 1.34x book (S17), with no visible capacitor premium.

Domestic power-capacitor makers such as Universal Cables (all-polypropylene LT/HT capacitors) could buy film locally as domestic supply scales (S19). ECMS-backed metallisers (Dhruv, Capfilm) add domestic demand for base film (S14, S15).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Polypropylene resin makes up 50-65% of production cost, and China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1). That caps pricing power for Indian entrants.

Capacitor film is a small, undisclosed share of revenue at all three producers. Commodity packaging-film cycles and leverage drive earnings: Cosmo's debt/equity is 1.04 (S17), and Jindal Poly's trailing net loss is Rs 991 cr (S18).
Jindal Poly's governance risk is building: two SEBI show-cause notices in 2026 (S8, S9), CRISIL ratings on Watch Negative, and Rs ~1,125 cr infused into JPFL since the fire (S10).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: SRF Q2 FY27 results and call: whether phase 2 has been capitalised and whether first KAPLAR revenue is reported (S11, S12).
Whether Cosmo First commissions its second metalliser and starts disclosing capacitor-film volumes (S4).
JPFL's line rebuilds (two lines due H2 FY27, one BOPP line by Q1 FY28) and confirmation of the capacitor-film doubling (S5, S10). Also the outcome of both SEBI notices (S8, S9).
Whether the government notifies DGTR's 30 Sep 2026 PET-film anti-dumping recommendation (S24). No duty specific to capacitor-grade BOPP has been found.

blocks.text: Capacitor-grade film is an ultra-thin dielectric film (the insulating layer between a capacitor's plates), mostly biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP). It is vacuum-metallised with aluminium or aluminium-zinc and wound into film capacitors. Cosmo First makes it in clean-room conditions with micro-slitting, at 2.5-12 micron thickness, for AC and DC capacitors used in industrial drives, power electronics, EVs and renewable systems (S3). Packaging BOPP has none of these requirements. SRF markets its KAPLAR grade on dielectric stability and self-healing performance (S12). Self-healing means a local short burns away the thin metal layer instead of destroying the capacitor.

Film makers are moving to thinner substrates that withstand higher voltages: IndexBox cites 2-4 micron grades for automotive use, especially 800-volt EV platforms. It sees BOPP holding 60-70% of volume and metallised film 40-50% of value (S1).

blocks.caption: Third-party forecasts (each is the publisher's own forecast)

blocks.text: The IndexBox and Mordor forecasts measure different things: film demand versus the value of finished capacitors. We could not open the Future Market Insights figure, so it is not included.

India is the world's 3rd-largest importer of capacitor metallised film, mostly from China, Japan and South Korea. China accounted for 7,867 shipments versus 588 for Japan (S16). These are shipment counts, not tonnes or value. We found no official tonnage series for the specific HS line.

New this week: on 30 Sep 2026 DGTR recommended anti-dumping duties of USD 54-366/t on PET film from Bangladesh, China and Thailand. Imports from those countries rose 186% over Apr 2024-Mar 2025, and the duty applies only once the government notifies it (S24). The coverage we read mentions no exclusion for electrical or capacitor grades. The case covers PET film, not BOPP, the main capacitor dielectric (S1).

blocks.text: After the Aug 2026 tranche, ECMS covers 106 approved applications with Rs 69,548 cr of investment and Rs 5,34,101 cr of projected production; 38 plants are already producing (S15). Each metallising or capacitor line approved adds domestic demand for base film, which today comes mostly from imports (S16).

blocks.text: Cosmo First: the capacitor range covers Al-Zn standard, pure Al, slope/RMF, segmented and 'series' metallised PP films; the company says the series grade targets renewable energy and EVs (S4). It does not disclose capacitor-film revenue. On Screener, trailing sales are Rs 4,004 cr, the stock trades at 13.0x P/E, and June-quarter sales rose 45.8% YoY. Those numbers reflect the packaging-film business (S17).

SRF: management said approvals had been secured from several leading customers. It expected early revenue towards the later part of Q2 FY27, and full capacity in Q1/Q2 of FY28 (S12). Against SRF's Rs 17,001 cr trailing sales (S25), the plant's ~Rs 283 cr total capex (S11) points to a small revenue contribution.

Jindal Poly Films: CRISIL says JPFL had 5,000 TPA of capacitor capacity before the fire and 5,000 TPA operational now. That suggests the capacitor line was restored early, but neither CRISIL nor any other source we found shows the planned doubling. Other figures from the rationale: 9M FY26 operating income of Rs 1,696 cr with an operating loss of Rs 51 cr; loss of profits not covered by insurance; Rs ~1,125 cr infused into JPFL since the fire (S10). Screener shows trailing sales of Rs 2,339 cr and a net loss of Rs 991 cr (S18).

blocks.title: Price-to-book of confirmed capacitor-film producers, 5 Oct 2026

blocks.text: None of the three companies reports capacitor-film volumes or revenue separately. Any 'share of revenue' figure is an estimate, not a disclosure.

items: Polyplex lists electrical insulation among its BOPET industrial uses, but we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S20). It is a possible beneficiary of the PET-film anti-dumping recommendation (S24).
UFlex / Flex Films sells BOPP, BOPET, CPP and metallised packaging films; we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S22).
Garware Hi-Tech Films makes polyester film for electrical and motor insulation at 10-350 micron (S21), thicker than the 2.5-12 micron capacitor band (S3).
Universal Cables makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and power-factor panels, a potential domestic film buyer (S19). We found no disclosed film-supply tie-up.
Syrma SGS is an ECMS beneficiary for passive-component inputs (copper-clad laminates, coils); we found no evidence that it buys capacitor film (S23).

blocks.text: Coverage gap: the main domestic film-capacitor makers (Deki, TDK India, Vishay India) and the ECMS metallisers (Dhruv, Capfilm) are unlisted or unconfirmed as listed (S14, S15). We found no listed mid-cap pure play, so the investable universe is narrow.

sections.title: Research house views and market pricing

subsections.title: Has the market priced it in?

blocks.text: Cosmo First trades on packaging-film earnings and Jindal Poly below book, and all three stocks sit 17-36% below their 52-week highs (S17, S18, S25). Neither valuation suggests a capacitor-film premium. We found no Indian broker note built around capacitor film; coverage of these companies is trade-press launch stories (S3, S5) and results summaries.

items: Resin cost: polypropylene makes up 50-65% of production cost (S1).
Chinese overcapacity: China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1) and supplies most of India's imports (S16).
Slow ramp-up: SRF took ~2.5 years from board approval (Oct 2023) to commissioning (May 2026) (S11) and expects full capacity only in FY28 (S12). JPFL's 2025 doubling target is unconfirmed (S5, S10).
Small share of revenue: packaging-film cycles dominate earnings (S17, S18).

Governance: Jindal Poly has two SEBI show-cause notices, dated Apr and Aug 2026, addressed to the company, its key managers, promoters and group entities. The company says the financial impact cannot yet be ascertained (S8, S9). CRISIL ratings are on Watch Negative (S10).
Q2 FY27 results (October): SRF's first KAPLAR revenue and phase-2 capitalisation (S11, S12).
Commissioning of Cosmo First's second metalliser (S4).
Restart of two more JPFL lines in H2 FY27 (S10) and confirmation of the capacitor-film doubling (S5).
ECMS metallised-film projects (Dhruv, Capfilm) coming on stream, which would add domestic demand for base film (S14, S15).
Localisation of EV and solar inverters, the segment IndexBox expects to grow 10-14% a year (S1).
Government notification of the PET-film anti-dumping duty (S24). A capacitor-BOPP-specific trade action has not been found.

companies.name: Cosmo First Ltd
companies.role: Makes metallised capacitor-grade BOPP (2.5-12 micron). Launched in Dec 2023 at ~750 MT/yr (S3); the metalliser is now rated at 900 MT/yr, with a second being prepared (S4).
companies.impact: The longest-running listed producer, but capacitor film is undisclosed and earnings track packaging film. P/E is 13.0x and debt/equity 1.04 (S17).

companies.name: Jindal Poly Films Ltd
companies.role: Its subsidiary JPFL Films makes capacitor film: 5,000 TPA is operational per CRISIL (S10), and a Rs 250 cr doubling citing a TDK testimonial was announced in 2024 (S5).
companies.impact: The fire recovery (~35% utilisation), the trailing loss and two 2026 SEBI notices outweigh the capacitor theme (S8, S9, S10, S18).

companies.name: SRF Ltd
companies.role: Commissioned a capacitor-grade BOPP (KAPLAR) plant at Indore on 15 May 2026 at ~Rs 277 cr (S11). Holds ECMS approval for a Rs 496 cr capacitor PP-film project (S13).
companies.impact: The largest new entrant, with customer approvals and early revenue guided for late Q2 FY27 (S12). The plant is immaterial to group earnings but adds competition for Cosmo and JPFL.

companies.name: Universal Cables Ltd
companies.role: Makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and APFC panels (S19).
companies.impact: A potential domestic film buyer; no film-supply tie-up is disclosed (S19).

companies.name: Polyplex Corporation Ltd
companies.role: BOPET film maker that lists electrical insulation among its industrial applications (S20).
companies.impact: Adjacent only: no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S20). The PET-film anti-dumping recommendation is more relevant to it (S24).

companies.name: UFlex Ltd
companies.role: Its Flex Films business makes BOPP, BOPET, CPP and metallised films (S22).
companies.impact: Has metallising know-how, but we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S22).

companies.name: Garware Hi-Tech Films Ltd
companies.role: Makes polyester film for electrical and motor insulation at 10-350 micron (S21).
companies.impact: Its thickness range sits above the capacitor band (S3), so the theme does not currently apply.

companies.name: Syrma SGS Technology Ltd
companies.role: ECMS beneficiary for passive-component inputs (copper-clad laminates, coils) (S23).
companies.impact: Part of the wider ECMS passive-component push (S15); not a confirmed capacitor-film buyer.

method: Weekly refresh of the 2026-W40 edition, researched on 6 Oct 2026 with web search and page fetches. We re-checked last week's claims on SRF, Cosmo First, JPFL, ECMS and SEBI. What changed: we added the CRISIL rating rationale of 18 May 2026 (JPFL's capacitor capacity, line restarts, infusions), the earlier SEBI show-cause notice of 27 Apr 2026, the Aug 2026 ECMS approval for Capfilm India, and DGTR's 30 Sep 2026 PET-film anti-dumping recommendation. Valuations were updated to Screener figures as of 5 Oct 2026. What we dropped: the Sector Alpha price page, a Multibagg note, the Bridge Chronicle and Indian Infrastructure ECMS items, and IndexBox's separate BOPP-only note; the data that still matters is covered by primary or newer sources. SRF's call transcript PDF, PIB and Business Standard pages could not be opened (certificate/403 errors), so SRF guidance is cited from search-result excerpts. We found no confirmation of SRF phase-2 capitalisation, JPFL's capacitor doubling, Cosmo's second metalliser, or a capacitor-BOPP-specific trade action, so none is stated as fact. Some company-website dates are access dates. Companies are classed 'other' unless a company or primary source confirms capacitor-grade production. No ratings or price targets are given.
